function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to pull live market data in real time.  
The most reliable way to get the current U.S. spot price of gold is to check a reputable financial news or market‑data website such as:

| Source | Typical URL |
|--------|-------------|
| Bloomberg | https://www.bloomberg.com/markets |
| Kitco | https://www.kitco.com/ |
| Reuters | https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities |
| CNBC | https://www.cnbc.com/commodities/ |

These sites update the spot price of gold (usually quoted in U.S. dollars per troy ounce) several times per minute during market hours.

**Approximate recent level (as of the last published data)**  
- Spot price: **≈ $2,200–$2,250 per troy ounce** (USD).  
- This figure is a snapshot from the most recent publicly available data and can fluctuate by a few dollars within minutes.

If you need the exact price for a specific time stamp, you’ll need to consult one of the live feeds above or use a financial data API (e.g., Bloomberg Terminal, Refinitiv, or a free API like Metals-API). Let me know if you’d like help setting up an API call or if you have any other questions!
